### 2026-10-06 – I worked on the schematics, importing libraries and having a bit of confusion on that because I initially didn't import the "Imported things" folder lol.

**1.73h**

I worked on the schematics, importing libraries and having a bit of confusion on that because I initially didn't import the "Imported things" folder lol.
Most of the time was working on cosmetics - I wanted to make something for LOL but wasn't sure, so after some internal debate, I chose the mastery symbol. Initially, I wasn't sure what cool things I could do with it until doing some research and realizing I could have shiny parts, different colors, etc etc. I was confused with how to get things "grayed out" and what the layers are for, but after fiddling around and doing research, I now know that each layer is essentially a different "layer" on the pcb where cool things could be added to get different textures and colors + properties (GND pour supposedly has some electrical effects if isolated?).
It was a fun session - tomorrow I will add the GND pour and silkscreen layers to make it look all cool + wire the pcb

I'm also worried about logging coding time - hackatime hasn't been working for me well? and in Lapse, it said most of my work was on a github repo I didn't work on. I'm quite confused - hopefully i'll get it sorted out.

### 2026-10-07 – I finished all the customization!!

**3h**

I finished all the customization!!
I wanted to add multiple colors and was thinking of doing so, so I researched how i could get it without paying premium (enig beautiful gold but expensive lol). So I used silkscreen for white (instead of original blue highlights) highlights, tightened up the edge cut to be closer to original shape, and added in the silk screen stuff. I also figured out what the F. and B. meant - and decided since the microcontroller and screens and whatnot were going to cover most of the design on the front, I would put the highlights in the back to show them.
Routing the pcbs were a chore lolll. I had to play the flow game with them, figuring out which paths I could take that wouldn't go on the sectioned out areas I had for the detailing (that I later decided I would put on the back so it didn't even matter). However, the unexpected good thing I got out of this was that I decided to put the copper routes to mimic the detailing I cannot put as actual different color. Hopefully this will turn out well, give it a cool techy look, if it even gives it a different look.
The extra half hour I'm adding as additional was the last half hour - I didn't even realize I paused it, but in this last half hour I finished up the silkscreen stuff and made the copper routes cooler and more purposeful to the detailing, so not shortest route lol. I think I  might have done some other stuff but those were probably just minor details then.
Next step - code! I hope my github and wakatime and whatnot will actually work so my code hours will be logged correctly - I'm not sure if I can reach 10 hours this week on this project, so maybe I will add a button or something?

tldr: added pcb designs + learned about gnd pour and silkscreen! Routed pcb (difficult, but used them as cosmetics as well based on route lol)

### 2026-10-08 – learned: single pole double throw switch

**3.05h**

learned: single pole double throw switch
learned: pos -> neg in circuit, need fuse (to break when too much voltage)
learned: what the 3.3V and 5V meant, and lithium battery 3.7V meaning
learned: difference btwn hard lithium and soft lithium batteries, mounting differences
learned: routing of battery + fuse + switch and how it works
learned: difference between dpdt, spdt, and spst switches (and that the c6 microcontroller doesn't support the battery stuff b/c it is simplified so I should use c3). I used spst at the end due to simplicity and mounting direction (spdt switches have the switch parallel to the pcb, like on the side, so it's harder to turn on and off where I wanted to place it. I initially thought dpdt would work but the guy in slack recommended spst and it works).

generally, I came into these sessions with new ideas - I wanted to add a battery and switch so it could function without the usb cable. The usbc port on the microcontroller can both data transfer and charge the connected battery, which was good. I did some research with AI, and after getting stuck on button orientation, which led to dpdt and errors in pcb when updating the pcb from the schematic, I asked for help (which I didn't record on timelapse) on the slack, joining the huddle and figuring it out. I hope the vias work - I don't know them very well. In the next 2.5 ish hours left, I want to finish the arduino coding!

I'm also not too satisfied with the aesthetics - I really wanted just the mastery symbol but had to edit it to an inspired trophy like thing. It makes me wonder if I should've went with the game's actually trophy type, with the esports' world championship coming up anyways. Anyways, I put too much time into the shape + routing it prettily, so I'll keep it like this.

The images include one of my errors before I asked for help and one of my work after the help. I'm asking for confirmation on the vias for their function - hopefully they work. Also, thank you to the guy who helped me search up good beginner hardware parts and tell me about the compatibility stuff between the microcontroller, switches, and batteries!

tldr: finished editing some cosmetics, added battery + switch + fuse with help, worked with vias and choosing parts

### 2026-10-11 – Today was quite unfortunate.

**2.37h**

Today was quite unfortunate.
I initially had a battery, so great. But, when getting parts for it, I realized that the lithium ion battery wouldn't be protected due to the size of the battery holder. If I wanted to change the footprint, the materials cost (of a protected battery, switch, fuse, battery holder) will exceed my budget, and I cannot pay the extra.
If i don't invest in a protected lithium battery, I would need to use this IC chip thing, or do software changes that, frankly, I'm incredibly not confident in. I don't have enough time today to actually research and figure out the IC thing, and considering the cost as well, it was difficult to implement.
So, I decided to scrap the battery.
The initial reason for the battery was so I could bring it to school and fiddle around with it. I could just connect it to my school chromebook if needed though.
I also didn't want to risk a safety hazard because of my incompetence in hardware assembling or in the design and materials itself. Perhaps for later projects, with more confidence and safety precautions, I would add a battery. For now, I just feel incredibly not confident about it, so I'm not gonna risk it.

Anyways, I also figured out the code for the pcb! I added 2 different sprites on top of customizing the initial state sprite. My sprite is a poro from League of Legends. When it is napping, the sprite will become a sleeping poro, and I did it by just adding the display line with an adjusted variable I created under the if statement of napping. Similarily (though there was no if statement. I just traced the logic of the code), I added a poro winking for the heart effect. Hopefully it works.

I want to add different trails depending on factors, but I do want to see the sparkle trail in person before choosing.

tldr: took off the battery system due to safety concerns and budget restraints. added customizations to the code outside of offered extensions in the project guidelines
